caseClassification.BEST_SUPPORTED: Status and content match what a strong hybrid coach would do in every material respect; only cosmetic or communication omissions.
caseClassification.ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE: A defensible coaching choice that differs from the best supported behaviour, or carries bounded non-material defects; no author concern materially triggered.
caseClassification.SUBOPTIMAL: Safe and serves the request, but a strong coach would materially do better: mis-dosed start, stalled trajectory, arrangement against a stated constraint, missed communication of a material trade-off, or a triggered author concern of moderate impact.
caseClassification.INSUFFICIENT_INFORMATION: The right answer was to ask or hold, and the engine did.
caseClassification.UNSUPPORTED: The engine could not serve a request it should serve, or served it wrongly (a program that cannot prepare the goal, contradicts the athlete's statements or evidence, or an excessive mutation).
caseClassification.CORPUS_ERROR: The failure is caused by the corpus or by something the interface cannot express; not counted against the runtime.

programClassification.PROGRAM_BEST_SUPPORTED: Phases, progression, quality timing, strength dose and loads, hybrid arrangement, event weeks, negotiation and week 1 are all sound.
programClassification.PROGRAM_ACCEPTABLE: Sound overall; bounded weaknesses in one or two dimensions.
programClassification.PROGRAM_SUBOPTIMAL: A material weakness a strong coach would fix before handing it over (stalled trajectory, mis-dosed start, arrangement against a constraint, missing pattern, ignored current doses).
programClassification.PROGRAM_INCOMPLETE: A trajectory the goal needs is missing or never reaches a necessary level; what is there is safe.
programClassification.PROGRAM_UNSUPPORTED: Wrong for the athlete as a whole (detrains or overloads, contradicts the evidence, or prescribes an event day the preparation cannot support).

readingRules: Judged as a strong hybrid running/strength coach: a safe ASK or a safe but under-built program is not credited as a positive prescription.

Envelopes and SSCTR conditions in force (R6-POLICY-2, records r6) are not re-decided; the weekly-review contract (unreported sessions reviewed as missed; unreviewed weeks keep the projection assumption, owned gap R18) is applied as approved.
Where the holdout skipped weekly reviews, the outcome is flagged R18-conditioned and, when material, separated by a counterfactual on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction.
Later changes are mapped from the dossiers only; a synthetic, non-holdout probe on the current unfrozen runtime is reported as informational and never as verification on this holdout.

cases.reason: Intermediate HM runner (210 min/4 days, 80-min long run, current 3x6 threshold, 115-min goal). The engine read a FULL wearable declaring 8 weeks whose rows cover only the last 10 days as 77 min/week over 1.5 days (EASY_LOW). The 16-week program never progresses: easy runs 15 min and long runs 30-35 min for 14 weeks, no quality session ever, then a 150-min half-marathon race; dumbbell RDL plus split squats every Saturday evening before the Sunday long run with no disclosure. The engine itself records LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET (35 of 105, materialToGoal) and requestedScopeSatisfied=false, yet returns PROPOSED with an empty negotiation. Corpus contribution is partial (the rows contradict the scenario's 'full history agrees'), but a counterfactual with eight consistent weeks on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction gives a sound HM program (204-260 min, long 75-105), and the stall and the silent proposal are runtime behaviour.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY: D50 (share-cap held long runs no longer count as the week's increase; flat-build stalls) and the D43/D47 EVENT_AMBITIOUS item. A synthetic thin-history probe on the current unfrozen runtime still yields 75 min/week, a 30-min first long run and a 40-min peak with only a non-blocking item, so the evidence-fusion defect is still open.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Fails every preferred element; triggers the concerns 'heavy lower body on Saturday evening before the long run' and 'starting her as a novice'.

cases.reason: Strength-led lifter: back squat 5x5 at 120 kg and bench 5x5 at 92.5 kg from documented loads at RIR 3, +2.5 kg steps (about 2%), consolidation weeks 4 and 8, accessory rotation at week 6 as requested; two easy runs, no quality, running about 40-56 min/week. Weaknesses: the squat emphasis is not honoured (squat once a week, hinge twice); a novice who jogs 25 min continuously is put on walk/jog (20-28 min) for 11 weeks and the Saturday longer run (up to 40) is never used.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: UNCLEAR: D42 changes the walk/jog start only for non-novices; no documented change for movement emphasis.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Matches the strength preferences and the running caution; misses squat emphasis and the 20-30 min continuous easy-run start; no concern triggered.

cases.reason: Never-runner, 10K finish in 12 weeks. Strength kept near current loads (back squat 4x6 at 85 kg, RIR 3) and race-week strength is light. Running is a walk/jog ladder reaching one 20-min continuous jog in week 9; the Sunday session never becomes longer than the others (max 28 min, gap '0 of 70' flagged as not material), the taper is 15-min easy runs, and race day is prescribed at 'hard but controlled (7-8/10)' with warm-up strides she never trained, contradicting the plan's own non-blocking 'completion with walk breaks' item. Twelve weeks is enough for a run/walk 10K build; the preparation is incomplete and the race-day prescription is wrong for this athlete (tissue-tolerance risk the author named).
cases.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY: D43(c) and D47 make race day a completion at conversational effort with walk breaks and strides only after executed strides, and state what the plan reaches. The slow ladder and the missing long run-walk trajectory: UNCLEAR (R12 concerns walk conversion only).
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Preferred continuous 25-40 min runs by weeks 6-8 and a 60-75 min Sunday session by weeks 9-10: not met; race-day effort contradicts the completion intent.

cases.reason: Experienced runner (330 min, long 105, current threshold 4x8 and HM-specific 2x20) adding first-ever strength, 88:00 goal. Good: running not reset (325-340), quality never Monday, a sound 10-14 day taper, novice strength at RIR 3 with 1-2 sets within equipment (no bench). Material misses: one key session a week although he currently does two; HM-specific work prescribed below his current session (2x12, 2x15, 3x12 against 2x20); long run flat at 105 for ten weeks (allowed to 140); the ambitious 88:00 is not flagged; strength selection is thin for a runner (no calf, hinge or single-leg work in most weeks, 24 of 30 min used).
cases.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY/UNCLEAR: D50 may lift some flat long-run weeks; nothing documented for current specific sessions, a second key session or time-goal realism.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: No concern triggered; three of four preferred elements only partly met.

cases.reason: Novice, 52, general fitness, offered 6 run and 4 strength days. Runs are correctly reduced to three walk/jog sessions with the other days as optional walks and an explanation, and day 0 = Wednesday is mapped correctly. But all four strength days are filled (upper/lower split for a novice), giving seven required sessions a week with three double days, exactly the author's concern; a 'PULL unavailable' note is shown although db-row is programmed every week.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: no documented change for strength-day selection or the pattern note.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Running subset matches; strength 'availability is not prescription' missed; concern '7 or more sessions/week, double days for a novice' triggered.

cases.reason: No wearable, no anchor: effort-based, no invented time, 120 min start, conservative threshold from week 3, long 50 to 70, taper; race on Saturday handled well (touch Tuesday, easy Thursday, rest Friday, race Saturday, rest Sunday). Kettlebell loads established by effort. Defects: no PULL exercise in any of 12 weeks although prone-row-practice (bodyweight) is in the library, with a false 'PULL unavailable' note; no optional calibration suggested; week-1 strength is a 12-min practice session.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: a synthetic kettlebell/bodyweight probe on the current unfrozen runtime still programs no pull exercise.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Matches the preferred run and race-week structure; strength misses the pull pattern; no concern triggered.

cases.reason: Self-report 200 min/long 75 versus a PARTIAL watch showing 95-127 min/long 55. The engine starts at 195 min with a 75-min long run (the author's first concern) while its own uncertainty text says 'the lower current exposure is used'. The trap-bar deadlift is correctly kept as history. The goblet squat reported as 20 kg TOTAL is prescribed as 20 kg PER_HAND (a load-convention error that can double the load), and the self-reported db-row and db-rdl loads are discarded and re-established. Quality introduced conservatively.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN for the start level. Convention: UNCLEAR; QRE-R6-01 (R6-POLICY-3 item 4) refuses convention mismatches in logs, but a synthetic probe on the current unfrozen runtime still labels a goblet squat PER_HAND.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Concern 'accepting 200 min/week and a 75-min long run at face value' triggered; conflict recorded but resolved the wrong way.

cases.reason: Experienced lifter, bodyweight and bands only, upper-body hypertrophy. Equipment respected and progression is by reps, never kilograms. But the program ignores his current doses (push-ups 2x8 against a current 3x20, split squat 2x10 against 3x15, band row established from scratch), keeps RIR 3 throughout (not close enough to failure for bodyweight hypertrophy), and does not carry the upper emphasis (lower-body sets about equal to upper). The Saturday run is 45 min, below his current 50, and never progresses; a false 'PULL unavailable' note is shown although band-row is programmed.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: no documented change for bodyweight current doses or emphasis.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Concern 'novice regressions instead of what he can do now' effectively triggered; equipment concerns respected.

cases.reason: 4-week 10K for a 4-month runner with a 50:00 hope (anchor predicts about 65). Good: three runs from week 1, no quality, light race-week strength, rest the day before. Misses: the long run is cut to 30 (below her current 35) and weekly running stays flat at 70; the unsupported 50:00 is not addressed beyond 'time goal is context only' (the author's concern 'silently accepting the 50-min target' is half-triggered: not used for pacing, but no expectation-setting); race day at 'hard but controlled'.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY/UNCLEAR: D50 may change flat weeks; time-goal realism OPEN.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Explicit negotiation on the time goal (preferred) missing; volume and long-run targets not met.

cases.reason: Balanced default offered, not demanded: quality Monday AM with the lower-body session that evening (hard day hard), Wednesday easy run plus a moderate full-body session, Friday upper-body on the eve of the long run, long run 60 to 75, known loads, consolidations every fourth week. Program-level weaknesses: no explanation of the trade-off or of the option to choose a temporary priority; hypertrophy kept at RIR 3 for 12 weeks.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN for the explanation.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Arrangement matches the preferred behaviour; the negotiation element is missing.

cases.reason: Two performance goals (45:00 10K from a 46:30 PR, back squat 5x3 at 140), three evenings, same-session stacking not confirmed. The engine proposes run plus strength back to back on all three evenings with only a non-blocking order confirmation and cost disclosures; priority is JOINT in build (no explicit temporary 10K priority); in build weeks a heavy barbell RDL 3x5 at 120 kg comes immediately before the Saturday long run in the same session; in specific weeks heavy squats follow the quality run; race week keeps a back-squat triple at the working load (RIR 4) four days out. Race on Saturday and the taper are handled.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: no documented change for same-session order or explicit priority.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Neither the preferred ASK nor the alternative's explicit priority; concern 'heavy squats before key runs' triggered; stacking disclosed rather than silent.

cases.reason: S1 missed quality: KEEP, no debt (best). S2 weekly: GATED_NEXT_STEP holds the missed quality step and, because the corpus did not report Tuesday's easy run (missed under the contract), trims easy and long runs by 5 min; it also cuts push-ups from 3x14 to 3x6 and dead-bugs 14 to 6 for the rest of the plan under ADVANCE gates (defect). S3 5-day work trip: minimal re-establishment (first quality slot easy, long run at the last completed 95), no ASK (best). Generated HM program is sound (199-245, long 80-105, threshold to HM-specific, taper).
cases.addressedByLaterChange: Bodyweight repetition collapse: PROBABLY (undocumented; a synthetic probe on the current unfrozen runtime no longer reproduces it, consistent with the D52 strength-state rework). S2 trims: contract behaviour.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: S1 and S3 match; S2 is a hold where the author preferred KEEP.

cases.reason: S1 missed Monday lower session: moved to Wednesday in place of the upper session, no stacking (a sound strength-first choice). S2 time-limited partial: KEEP, not treated as fatigue. S3: small set holds on RDL, calf and trunk because the partial session's content could not be expressed (interface gap). Generated strength-first program uses known loads with 2.5 kg steps and consolidations; easy running flat at 20/30 min (fine for a general goal).

cases.reason: S1 single under-target quality: KEEP (best). S2: holds the quality step (acceptable). S3 second adverse quality: KEEP (acceptable). S4 third consecutive under-target quality with impaired next-day function and a harder long run: KEEP, deferring to a week-end gate, with no cross-week pattern named and no check-in. R18-conditioned: the holdout skipped the week-5 weekly review; on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction that review gives QUALITY REGRESS and LONG HOLD, so the pattern is answered at weekly cadence. Residual gap: no mid-week response to impaired function and no check-in.

cases.reason: The narrative says every strength session felt easier with reps in reserve to spare, but the facts use AS_PRESCRIBED, which copies the planned reserve, so every log shows RIR 3 = prescribed. FREEZE-1's strength EARNED rule keys on logged reserve above the prescription, so no earned step could fire. S1/S2 KEEP are appropriate (the plan already adds 2.5 kg in week 2); S3's reason text ('one easier execution') misdescribes eight consistent reports and nothing asks about the label/log conflict. Generated program: strength-first, known loads, small steps.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: S3 preferred MODIFY not met, but the corpus did not supply the evidence the interface could carry (exercise RIR).

cases.reason: S1 local quad soreness: removes the optional split-squat accessory; Tuesday's run was already easy; not clinical. S2 systemic fatigue: the remaining quality becomes easy and the strength session drops about 40% of its sets at RIR 4; the long run is left unchanged and there is no check-in on sleep, stress or illness. S3 recovered: KEEP at a week-5-level dose (no catch-up).
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: Matches preferred/alternative behaviour except the long-run reduction and the check-in in S2.

cases.reason: S1 unavailable Sunday: long run moved to Saturday replacing the easy run, Sunday skipped (best). S2: holds the long-run step although the long run was executed (unnecessary) and collapses bodyweight reps. S3 permanent schedule change from 2027-03-01: re-mapped from the effective date with quality on Wednesday and the race kept, but the full-body session with dumbbell RDL 3x10 and step-ups lands on Saturday, the eve of every Sunday long run, for the remaining eight weeks, with no cost disclosed (author concern). S4 KEEP. The generated HM program is sound.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN for the arrangement; bodyweight collapse PROBABLY (see R6-H17).

cases.reason: A one-day double conflict (from = to = Tuesday 2027-09-28, strength AM, sameTurnConfirmed:false). The engine treats it as a permanent shift change: the conflict date itself is untouched (strength stays on the evening he cannot do), and from the next week strength is stacked with the Tuesday run in the same morning against his statement, with quality moved to Thursday. In the holdout run (no weekly reviews for weeks 0-3) the rearrangement also cut running to 45-50 min/week with 15-20-min long runs for weeks 5-9 (R18-conditioned: absent on the reconstruction when weeks 0-3 are reviewed). S2's weekly review restores running. The stacking and the untouched date reproduce on a synthetic probe on both the FREEZE-1 reconstruction and the current unfrozen runtime.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: QRE-R6-08 adds schedule-change validation only; the temporary-turn semantics are unchanged on the current runtime (synthetic probe). Running collapse: R18 owned gap.

cases.reason: S1 two-week bodyweight-only travel: pattern-matched substitutes (box squat, push-up, glute bridge, reverse lunge, calf raise, dead-bug) only inside 2027-05-03..16, running untouched, originals back afterwards; but no pull substitute (prone-row-practice exists; disclosed as 'without a substitute'). cases.reason: S1 goal change to a 10K with strength maintenance: future phases re-planned from the effective date (quality, long run 55-70, taper, post-race recovery), strength volume about 30% lower with loads held, earlier weeks untouched (sound). S2 race moved two weeks earlier: the race, taper and post-race weeks move correctly, but the four weeks before the race collapse to 15-25-min runs (45-83 min/week, 15-30-min long runs) from a runner doing 148-158 min with 65-70-min long runs. R18-conditioned: the holdout reviewed none of weeks 0-5; on the reconstruction with those weeks reviewed, the same replan gives 148/158/158/111 min and a 70-min long run.
cases.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN (R18 owned gap). The QRE-R6-09 ceiling change (entry ceiling in every projected week when the 30-day window has no run) points the same way.
cases.comparedToAuthorAssessment: S1 matches; S2 structure matches but the dose is the opposite of 'compressed with a lower peak'. R18-adjusted classification: ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE.

cases.reason: S1 KEEP. S2 17-day vacation: re-establishment without ASK; week 9 at about 60% of the pre-pause volume with quality converted to easy and a 65-min long run, strength 2x8 from log at RIR 3 (within the author's ranges); but the four-day stub week opens with a 20-min long run, and the plan returns to the full prior dose (quality plus a 95-min long run, +55%) in the third week with the peak unchanged; no time-goal note. But running plateaus at 105 min/week with a 45-min long run from week 7, no quality at all in 12 weeks for an experienced runner, and race day at 'hard but controlled' with strides while the item says 'completion with walk breaks'.

learningMetrics.observation: No learned pattern changed any decision on the holdout. Progression responses came from week-local gates (HOLD/REGRESS), not from the Athlete Model.

findings.title: Cold-start evidence fusion between wearable history and self-report fails in both directions
findings.evidence: R6-H01: FULL completeness with 8 declared weeks but rows covering 10 days is read as 77 min/week over 1.5 days for a 210-min runner. R6-H07: PARTIAL history (95-127 min) is overridden by the 200-min self-report while the uncertainty text claims the lower exposure is used. Counterfactual: H01 with 8 consistent weeks gives a sound program.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: no documented change; a synthetic thin-history probe on the current unfrozen runtime reproduces the H01 reading (75 min/week, long 30, peak 40).

findings.title: Progression stalls: long-run and easy-run trajectories go flat or never build
findings.evidence: R6-H01 easy 15 / long 30-35 for 14 weeks; R6-H34 HM long 80-85 and flat weekly volume for 14 weeks (engine's own horizon: peak 85 vs target 105); R6-H27 plateau at 105 min and a 45-min long run from week 7; R6-H09 long run cut below current and flat; R6-H03 no Sunday progression; R6-H04 long run flat at 105.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY: D50 (share-cap holds no longer consume the week's increase; author probe S: 47 of 66 programs with 4+ flat build weeks to 0). Not verifiable on this holdout; the synthetic thin-history HM on the current runtime still peaks at 40 min.

findings.title: DOUBLE_CONFLICT: a one-day turn conflict becomes a permanent same-turn stack and the conflict date is not resolved
findings.evidence: R6-H23 S1 with changes {strengthTurn:AM, sameTurnConfirmed:false, from=to=one Tuesday}: the conflict evening keeps its strength session; every later Tuesday stacks strength and the run in the same morning; quality moves to Thursday. Reproduced by a synthetic probe on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction and on the current unfrozen runtime.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: QRE-R6-08 adds schedule-change validation only.

findings.title: Replan and rearrangement paths read unreviewed weeks as zero exposure and collapse running before a race (R18-conditioned)
findings.evidence: R6-H25 S2: 15-25-min runs for the four weeks before a 10K; R6-H23 S1: 45-50 min/week for weeks 5-9. The projection assumes those weeks were executed (R18), the replan assumes nothing was. With the skipped weekly reviews supplied on the reconstruction neither collapse occurs.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: R18 is an owned gap (Engineering with Product/Data); the QRE-R6-09 single-run ceiling change applies the 15-min entry in every projected week when the 30-day window is empty, which points the same way.

findings.title: A program is PROPOSED although the engine records that it cannot prepare the goal, with no negotiation
findings.evidence: R6-H01: LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET (35 of 105, materialToGoal) and requestedScopeSatisfied=false, negotiation empty, then a 150-min race; R6-H03: '0 of 70' marked not material.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: PARTLY: D43/D47 build EVENT_AMBITIOUS_FOR_CURRENT_RUNNING with what the plan reaches (present in the synthetic current probe) but it stays non-blocking (R8 open).

findings.title: Race day prescribed at race effort with strides for athletes whose plan built only walk/jog or a restart (safety-relevant)
findings.evidence: R6-H03 never-runner, longest continuous 20 min, races 10K at 7-8/10 with warm-up strides never trained; R6-H27 restart athlete likewise; both carry a 'completion with walk breaks' item that contradicts the prescription.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: ADDRESSED_PER_DOSSIER: D43(c) and D47 (race-day completion basis, strides only after executed strides). Cannot be verified on this holdout.

findings.title: Load convention: a goblet squat reported as 20 kg TOTAL is prescribed as 20 kg PER_HAND; self-reported known loads are dropped when wearable strength rows exist (safety-relevant)
findings.evidence: R6-H07 week 0 goblet-squat KNOWN 20 kg PER_HAND (self-report TOTAL); db-row and db-rdl re-established. A synthetic probe on both runtimes labels a goblet squat PER_HAND.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: UNCLEAR: QRE-R6-01 (R6-POLICY-3 item 4) refuses convention mismatches in logs; the intake merge and the goblet-squat convention are still PER_HAND on the current runtime (synthetic).

findings.title: Hybrid arrangement places loaded lower-body work just before the long run without disclosure
findings.evidence: R6-H01 RDL and split squats every Saturday evening before the Sunday long run; R6-H16 heavy RDL 3x5 at 120 kg immediately before the Saturday long run in the same session (build weeks); R6-H22 S3 full-body RDL session moved onto the eve of the long run after a schedule change.

findings.title: Known current doses are under-used at cold start
findings.evidence: R6-H08 push-ups 2x8 against a current 3x20, RIR 3 throughout for experienced bodyweight hypertrophy; R6-H04 HM-specific work below the current 2x20 and one key session instead of two; R6-H02 walk/jog for a continuous 25-min jogger.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: no documented change (D42 applies to non-novice walk/jog starts only).

findings.title: Availability treated as prescription for strength in a novice
findings.evidence: R6-H05: four strength sessions plus three walk/jog sessions required, three double days, for a 52-year-old novice; run days were correctly reduced.

findings.title: Bodyweight repetitions collapse after a gated review
findings.evidence: 18 step proposals reduce bodyweight repetitions for the rest of the plan under ADVANCE gates (R6-H17 S2 push-up 3x14 to 3x6, dead-bug 14 to 6; R6-H22, R6-H24, R6-H26, R6-H31-35).
findings.addressedByLaterChange: PROBABLY (undocumented): a synthetic probe reproduces it on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction (dead-bug 1x12 to 1x6) but not on the current unfrozen runtime (1x12 kept), consistent with the D52 strength-state rework. No dossier names it; not verifiable on this holdout.

findings.title: PULL pattern: the bodyweight pull option is never selected and the 'PULL unavailable' note is unreliable
findings.evidence: R6-H06 12 weeks without any pull exercise (prone-row-practice is BODYWEIGHT); R6-H24 substitution window without pull; R6-H05 and R6-H08 show 'PULL unavailable' while db-row or band-row is programmed.
findings.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN: the synthetic kettlebell/bodyweight probe on the current runtime still programs no pull.

findings.title: Correction chains and race records lose or downgrade executed work
findings.evidence: R6-H32 S2 correction rejected as INVALID_CORRECTION_CHAIN; R6-H30 S5 an accepted correction is excluded and the race row disappears from the carried ledger; races finished faster than the planned duration are recorded PARTIAL and non-comparable (R6-H29, R6-H30; synthetic current probe still PARTIAL).
findings.addressedByLaterChange: Corrections: PLAUSIBLY by R6-POLICY-3 item 8 (QRE-R6-13/14: append-only record, a correction resolves a conflict), UNCLEAR. Race PARTIAL: OPEN.

findings.title: Athlete Model is inert on the holdout
findings.evidence: In all three consent cases no learned pattern changed a decision; R6-H34's three identical long-run responses produce gate holds and a regress but nothing athlete-specific; the model's pattern scope is arrangement only (FREEZE-1 r6-adaptation LEARNED_REARRANGEMENT).
findings.addressedByLaterChange: OPEN (design scope; QRE-R6-16 consent fix does not add learning).

findings.title: Two-goal, three-evening athlete gets unconfirmed stacking, JOINT priority and poor session order
findings.evidence: R6-H16: run plus strength on all three evenings with a non-blocking order question, no explicit 10K priority until SPECIFIC, heavy hinge before the long run, heavy squat after quality, a working-load squat triple four days before the race.

findings.title: No mid-week response or check-in to a third adverse key session with impaired next-day function
findings.evidence: R6-H19 S4 KEEP; the counterfactual shows the skipped week-5 weekly review would have regressed quality (R18).

findings.title: Time-goal realism is never communicated
findings.evidence: R6-H09 50:00 against an anchor predicting about 65; R6-H04 88:00; R6-H16 45:00: only 'time goal is context only'.

findings.title: Stated emphasis preferences not carried into the dose
findings.evidence: R6-H02 squat emphasis (squat once a week, hinge twice); R6-H08 upper emphasis (lower sets about equal).

findings.title: Small communication and record defects
findings.evidence: R6-H15 no trade-off or temporary-priority explanation; R6-H13 no obstetric routing in the UNSUPPORTED reason; R6-H22 S2 long-run hold after an executed (moved) long run; R6-H17 a missed session recorded with ledger status PARTIAL; R6-H21 S2 long run not reduced under systemic fatigue and no check-in.

fundamentalHoleAssessment.summary: No fundamental architecture hole: every family is handled by an identifiable mechanism (gated conditional projection, weekly review gates, provenance, clinical routing, substitution windows, event-week rules), clinical and scope routing is 100% correct, and 47 of 52 assessable steps are appropriate. The failures are not bounded edge coverage either: they sit in core semantics that every V1 athlete passes through: cold-start evidence fusion (CQ-R6-01), long-run/easy progression (CQ-R6-02), the state used by replans for unreviewed weeks (CQ-R6-04, R18), conflict semantics (CQ-R6-03), and an Athlete Model that learns nothing beyond arrangement (CQ-R6-14). Each is localized to a rule set and fixable without re-architecture, but none is an edge case.

kmpCriteria.criterion: Cold start works for core V1 profiles
kmpCriteria.note: Works for the standard intermediate self-reported runner (17 of 18 sequence-case generations acceptable or better) and for known-load lifters; fails or is materially suboptimal for 7 of the 9 dedicated cold-start profiles (wearable conflict, novice racer, experienced runner adding strength, bodyweight hypertrophy, short-horizon race) plus the restart (H27).

30 of 30 PROPOSED programs are structurally complete with phases, taper, race week and post-event weeks; 20 of 30 are acceptable or better, 8 suboptimal, 1 incomplete, 1 unsupported; the engine proposes programs it marks as unable to prepare the goal.

kmpCriteria.criterion: Balanced no longer has structural suboptimal behaviour
kmpCriteria.note: The no-priority default (H15) is arranged correctly; the two-performance-goal, three-evening case (H16) shows unconfirmed stacking, JOINT priority without an explicit choice and heavy hinge before the long run in the same session.

kmpCriteria.criterion: Run, strength and hybrid trajectories are materially complete
kmpCriteria.note: Standard HM/10K run trajectories and known-load strength progressions are complete; long-run stalls, novice race builds, bodyweight hypertrophy dosing, the missing pull pattern and eve-of-long-run lower-body placement are not.

A 5-day break resumes with a minimal re-establishment; a 17-day break re-enters at about 60% and is gated by evidence; an 11-week restart starts from current running; no ASK when a nonclinical category is given; illness routes to a human. Caveats: a fast conditional third week and an unchanged peak in H26; H27's plateau is counted under trajectories.

kmpCriteria.criterion: Supported event profiles include the race-week transition
kmpCriteria.note: Every event program carries taper, race week (touch at 3+ days, optional shakeout, light or no strength in the final days, Saturday races handled) and post-event weeks; event-week conflicts are resolved by subtraction; but completion athletes get a race-effort race day (H03, H27; addressed per dossier by D43/D47) and race results are recorded PARTIAL.

The temporary equipment window substitutes by pattern, leaves running untouched, survives a time-zone change and reverts; the bodyweight pull option is never found (H24 window, H06 for 12 weeks). Only one substitution case in the holdout.

kmpCriteria.criterion: The Athlete Model changes future decisions without obvious overfit
kmpCriteria.note: No overfit and no false causal claim, but no learned pattern changed any decision; H34's repeated long-run response was handled by week-local gates only; H20 is a corpus error.

kmpCriteria.criterion: The fresh holdout reveals no fundamental architecture or domain hole
kmpCriteria.note: No architecture hole; core-semantics domain defects in cold-start evidence fusion, progression, unreviewed-week state (R18) and conflict semantics.

kmpCriteria.criterion: Remaining gaps are bounded edge coverage rather than core semantics
kmpCriteria.note: The leading gaps (CQ-R6-01 to CQ-R6-05) concern evidence fusion, progression and state semantics every athlete passes through.

verdict.rationale: On FREEZE-1, adaptation decisions are mostly sound (47 of 52 assessable steps appropriate, including both ASK/clinical steps; all intake ASK, scope and clinical routing correct; robust data-quality handling), but cold start fails or is materially suboptimal for 7 of 9 dedicated profiles, 10 of 30 programs need material fixes, two adaptation event types (one-day double conflict; event-date replans over unreviewed weeks) produce unsupported proposals, and the Athlete Model learns nothing. Several defects are safety-relevant in a shadow setting (race-effort race day after walk/jog preparation; a TOTAL load re-labelled PER_HAND). Some findings are addressed per the dossiers (D43/D47, D50, plausibly R6-POLICY-3 item 8, the bodyweight collapse on the current runtime) but none can be verified on this holdout because there is no frozen post-fix runtime; others reproduce on the current unfrozen runtime with synthetic inputs (CQ-R6-01, -03, -07, -12, race PARTIAL). This assessment informs the readiness verdicts; it does not set them.

recommendedVerdicts.COACHING_DECISION_QUALITY: NOT_READY: adaptation decision core is close (bounded fixes: double-conflict semantics, R18 state, correction chains), but cold-start decisions are not at coach quality.
recommendedVerdicts.WHOLE_PROGRAM_QUALITY: NOT_READY: 20 of 30 programs acceptable or better, concentrated in one profile; stalls, evidence-fusion errors and arrangement defects in the rest.

limitations: The judge is an AI agent applying expert coaching judgment; there is no human, empirical or clinical validation, and nothing here is a claim of one.
Families are small (2-9 cases); the distribution describes this holdout, not a population.

The holdout skipped many weekly reviews; outcomes depending on unreviewed weeks are flagged R18-conditioned. Counterfactuals separating R18 effects were run only on the FREEZE-1 reconstruction (four controls reproduced the recorded results exactly); the reconstruction's SSCTR records file is the archived r6 copy, not byte-identical to the frozen file, but it yields the same authority.

Later changes are mapped from the dossiers only. Synthetic, non-holdout probes on the current unfrozen runtime are informational; they are not a holdout rerun, not a verification of any later change on this holdout, and not frozen evidence.

Interface gaps recorded by the holdout author (partial strength content, stale sync, turn-level conflict, last-day next-day function) limit what some steps could express; they were taken into account case by case and only R6-H20 was judged a corpus error.
The topic docs in CoachingCore/r6/*.md were not read; envelopes and SSCTR conditions were not re-decided.

The judge reconstructed FREEZE-1 under reviews/coaching-quality/freeze1-recon/ for the counterfactuals and deleted it afterwards; build-freeze1-reconstruction.mjs recreates it and freeze1-recon-manifest.json records the verification.
